_notes: Format follows plan section 5. Each step: year in the cycle, crop slug, sow_month, harvest_month.
A harvest_month smaller than sow_month means the crop is harvested in the next calendar year (it spans into the next cycle year).
companion: true marks a crop sown into a standing crop (for example red clover underseeded in oats); overlaps with it are allowed.
Subtropical templates are APPROXIMATE for Sindh and Punjab; review with local farmers or extension staff.

templates.name: Corn–soybean
templates.description: The common two-year rotation in central Iowa. Strong markets and familiar equipment, but the soil is bare from harvest to planting and there are only two crop families.

templates.name: Sorghum–soybean–winter wheat + rye cover
templates.description: Swaps maize for drought-tolerant sorghum, adds winter wheat so the field is covered over winter, and a rye cover after wheat. Lower summer water demand and less bare soil.

templates.name: Corn + rye cover–soybean–oats with red clover
templates.description: Adds a winter rye cover after corn, a small grain (oats) to break the corn–soybean pest cycle, and red clover underseeded in the oats to fix nitrogen and add organic matter.

templates.name: Cotton–wheat
templates.description: The common annual double crop in Sindh and southern Punjab: kharif cotton then rabi wheat. High water use from cotton and only grass/cotton families.

templates.name: Rice–wheat
templates.description: Alternative current rotation for central Punjab: kharif rice then rabi wheat. Very high water use and puddling damages soil structure.

templates.name: Sorghum–chickpea / cotton–wheat
templates.description: Halves the cotton area: every other year grows drought-tolerant sorghum in kharif and chickpea on residual moisture in rabi. Cuts seasonal water demand and adds a nitrogen-fixing pulse.

templates.name: Cotton–berseem / mungbean–wheat
templates.description: Replaces one wheat crop with berseem (winter fodder legume), then a kharif mungbean sown in July and wheat. Two legumes per cycle, more families, less water. Retimed 2026-11-15: the earlier April mungbean and July maize flowered in peak heat (more critical heat alerts than the current rotation in Faisalabad and Sindh).
